literal: " Lin knelt and answered: "Filial piety is of my house; wealth and honor are grace from Your Majesty."
idiomatic: Lin knelt: "Filial piety is our house's gift; wealth and honor are Your Majesty's grace."

literal: " In the fifth year he was Inspector of Eastern Yan and again brought Lady Feng's household troops.
idiomatic: In the fifth year he was Inspector of Eastern Yan and again brought Feng's household troops.

literal: Because of Lady Feng's sorcery he lost much clarity of mind; soon he suffered hemiplegia.
idiomatic: Feng's sorcery cost him his wits; soon hemiplegia struck.

literal: Lady Feng's bribes lay in heaps; the censorate impeached her — she and Lin were both summoned and handed to the Minister of Justice.
idiomatic: Feng's bribes heaped up; the censorate impeached — both were handed to the Minister of Justice.

literal: Many prisoners lay with her; in the prison they vied for her favor.
idiomatic: Many prisoners lay with her; in prison they fought for her.

literal: Soon a separate edict beheaded Lady Feng in the market and cut her corpse into nine parts.
idiomatic: Soon an edict beheaded Feng in the market and cut her into nine.

literal: Lin died of illness in prison.
idiomatic: Lin died of illness in prison.

literal: Lin had read widely and also had literary ornament.
idiomatic: Lin read widely and wrote with ornament.

literal: From the Zhongxing era to Xiaowu, most edicts, mandates, memorials, and proclamations were Lin's work.
idiomatic: From Zhongxing to Xiaowu most edicts and proclamations were Lin's.

literal: Yet he was extravagant, addicted to wealth and women, and among his brothers did not fully keep harmonious kinship — the age criticized him for it.
idiomatic: Yet he was extravagant, greedy for wealth and women, and not fully kind among brothers — the age faulted him.

literal: He had long been at odds with Wei Shou; when Shou later monopolized the national history, Lin feared slander and therefore pleased him: "In the past there was Ban Gu; today there is Master Wei."
idiomatic: Long at odds with Wei Shou, when Shou took the national history Lin feared slander and flattered him: "Once Ban Gu — today Master Wei."

literal: Shou snorted through his nose; the resentment did not lift.
idiomatic: Shou snorted; the grudge did not lift.

literal: Lin's son Zhan.
idiomatic: Lin's son was Zhan.

literal: Zhan, styled Yantong, was pure and white, fine in bearing, spirit and color lofty; he did not speak rashly — in talent and grace he was the finest of the younger generation.
idiomatic: Zhan, styled Yantong, was pure, fine in bearing, spirit lofty, speech careful — the finest of the younger generation.

literal: At first Xun Ji of Yingchuan came from the south into Luoyang; Zhan studied under Ji and therefore had classics and histories with proper masters.
idiomatic: At first Xun Ji of Yingchuan came from the south; Zhan studied under him and gained proper masters in the classics.

literal: Attendant Li Shenjun had elegant repute; in his later years without a son, seeing Zhan, he sighed to Xing Shao: "Yesterday I saw Cui Lin's son — at once first among the rising generation."
idiomatic: Attendant Li Shenjun, childless in old age, saw Zhan and sighed to Xing Shao, "Yesterday I saw Lin's son — first among the rising generation."

literal: " I have no such thing; seeing this wounds the heart!"
idiomatic: I have no such son — the sight wounds the heart!"

literal: At fifteen Inspector Gao Ang summoned him as Chief Clerk; Prince of Qinghe Gao Yue declined him as Sacrificer of the Western Pavilion of the Opening Office.
idiomatic: At fifteen Inspector Gao Ang made him Chief Clerk; Prince Gao Yue of Qinghe declined him as Western Pavilion Sacrificer.

literal: Cui Xuan of Boling as Commandant of Justice memorialized him as Attending Censor.
idiomatic: Cui Xuan of Boling as Commandant memorialized him Attending Censor.

literal: Because his father and Xuan were at odds, he soon left office.
idiomatic: Father and Xuan were at odds; he soon left office.

literal: Shenwu summoned him with Prince of Beihai Xi as companions to the princes, then made him Middle Army Officer of the Chancellor's Office and Chief Clerk.
idiomatic: Shenwu made him and Prince Xi companions to the princes, then Middle Army Officer and Chief Clerk.

literal: When Wenxiang died the death was kept secret; Wenxuan ordered Zhan Acting Chief Clerk of the Chancellor's Office and sent him to Ye.
idiomatic: Wenxiang died with the news sealed; Wenxuan made Zhan Acting Chief Clerk and sent him to Ye.

literal: Emperor Xiaojing of Wei on the Human Day ascended the Cloud Dragon Gate.
idiomatic: Wei Emperor Xiaojing on the Human Day climbed the Cloud Dragon Gate.

literal: With his father Lin he attended the feast and composed verse.
idiomatic: He and father Lin attended the feast and made verse.

literal: An edict asked Xing Shao and others: "How does young Zhan's poem compare with his father's?"
idiomatic: An edict asked Xing Shao and others how young Zhan's poem compared with his father's.

literal: " All said: "Lin is broad, elegant, and grand; Zhan's tone is fresh — both are crowns among poets."
idiomatic: All said, "Lin is broad and grand; Zhan's tone is fresh — both crown poets."

literal: " When the feast ended all sighed in praise, saying: "Today's banquet is wholly for father and son Zhan of Cui."
idiomatic: When the feast ended all sighed, "Today's banquet is wholly for the Cui father and son."

literal: " Yang Yin wished to bring Zhan into the Secretariat; Lu Sidao then served in the Secretariat — Yin asked the relative merit of their literary craft; Sidao said: "Cui Zhan's literary beauty truly deserves praise, but the age values his grace, and therefore his talent is buried."
idiomatic: Yang Yin wished Zhan for the Secretariat; Lu Sidao served there; Yin asked their merit; Sidao said, "Zhan's beauty deserves praise, but the age values his grace and buries his talent."

literal: " Yin said: "This speech has reason."
idiomatic: Yin said, "That has reason."

literal: " That day he memorialized for appointment.
idiomatic: That day he was memorialized for appointment.

literal: Yin also said: "In Jin times Pei Zan was Secretariat Attendant — spirit lofty; each time he passed the forbidden gate the guards were solemnly moved."
idiomatic: Yin also said, "In Jin Pei Zan was Secretariat Attendant — spirit lofty; passing the forbidden gate guards stirred."

literal: " Cui Sheng is likewise grand — he should not shame Master Pei?"
idiomatic: Cui Sheng is likewise grand — he should not shame Master Pei?"

literal: In the first year of Huangjian he was made Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: In Huangjian's first year he was Regular Attendant.

literal: With Li Gai of Zhao he was a sworn friend.
idiomatic: With Li Gai of Zhao he was sworn friend.

literal: When Gai was to return east, Zhan sent him a letter: "Blowing off steam with wine is my constant fault; railing and cutting to the quick is especially yours."
idiomatic: When Gai returned east Zhan wrote, "Wine and swagger are my fault; railing and cutting are especially yours."

literal: " You go home — where shall I hear my faults?"
idiomatic: You go home — where shall I hear my faults?"

literal: " Zhan suffered from qi blockage and was by nature slow and heavy; though he held posts in both secretariats, he could not bear to memorialize at court.
idiomatic: Zhan suffered blocked qi and was slow by nature; though in both secretariats he could not bear to memorialize.

literal: When Xiaozhao took the throne the heir apparent took his tutor; Zhan was made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and summoned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: When Xiaozhao reigned the heir took tutors; Zhan was Junior Mentor and summoned to Jinyang.

literal: The edict said: "The Eastern Palace is young and not yet steeped in teaching."
idiomatic: The edict said, "The Eastern Palace is young and not steeped in teaching."

literal: " Your bearing and wind are a man's model; therefore I trouble you to dwell day and night, opening the young mind."
idiomatic: Your bearing is a man's model; dwell day and night and open the young mind."

literal: " One thing, three goods — all are entrusted to you."
idiomatic: One thing, three goods — all entrusted to you."

literal: " Zhan devoted himself to the Eastern Palace; nurture, lecturing, and the etiquette of coming and going were all entrusted to him.
idiomatic: Zhan devoted himself to the Eastern Palace — nurture, lecture, and ritual of coming and going.

literal: When the heir took Lady Hulu as consort, an edict ordered Zhan and Grand Herald Cui Li to draft the marriage rites and notes — the supervising offices took them as later models.
idiomatic: When the heir wed Lady Hulu, Zhan and Grand Herald Cui Li drafted marriage rites — offices took them as models.

literal: At the time an edict debated the rites of the Three Revered; the Heir Apparent's Junior Tutor Wei Shou made one opinion — courtiers none failed to echo it.
idiomatic: An edict debated the Three Revered; Junior Tutor Wei Shou made one opinion — courtiers echoed.

literal: Zhan set out a separate opinion; when Shou finished reading he laughed and said nothing.
idiomatic: Zhan set a separate opinion; Shou read, laughed, and was silent.

literal: Zhan said with stern face: "The Sage has charged the ministers to debate the great canon of state; the Junior Tutor's name and standing are not light — if Zhan's opinion stands, praise what is strong;
idiomatic: Zhan said sternly, "The Sage charged us to debate the state canon; the Junior Tutor is not light — if my opinion stands, praise what is strong;

literal: if not, probe what is wanting."
idiomatic: if not, probe what fails."

literal: How may one read a fellow countryman's proposed text and only laugh coldly?"
idiomatic: How may one read a countryman's text and only laugh coldly?"

literal: " Cui Zhan holds a lofty post in the holy court and still is not free of fault — how may plain scholars hope to advance!"
idiomatic: Cui Zhan in a lofty post still is faulted — how may plain scholars advance!"

literal: " Zhan's countenance was square and stern, his words heroic in debate;
idiomatic: Zhan's countenance was square and stern, his words heroic;

literal: Shou flushed and hastened away — in the end not a word.
idiomatic: Shou flushed and fled — not a word.

literal: Zhan was simple and proud, proud of talent and standing; those he associated with were all famous in the age.
idiomatic: Zhan was simple and proud of talent; his circle were all names of the age.

literal: At the Censorate he always had food sent from home, with every delicacy;
idiomatic: At the Censorate food came from home with every delicacy;

literal: in a separate room he ate alone — at ease as if it were natural.
idiomatic: in a separate room he ate alone — easy as nature.

literal: A man of Hedong surnamed Pei was also a censor; watching Zhan eat, he went to visit.
idiomatic: A Hedong man surnamed Pei was also censor; watching Zhan eat, he visited.

literal: Zhan did not speak with him and did not offer spoon or chopsticks.
idiomatic: Zhan did not speak and offered no spoon or chopsticks.

literal: Pei sat watching until Zhan finished eating and withdrew.
idiomatic: Pei sat watching until Zhan finished and left.

literal: The next day he brought his own spoon and chopsticks and ate freely.
idiomatic: Next day he brought his own utensils and ate freely.

literal: Zhan said: "At first I did not call you to eat, nor speak with you — yet you were not bound by small niceties."
idiomatic: Zhan said, "I did not call you to eat nor speak — yet you were not bound by small niceties."

literal: " In the past Liu Yi at Jingkou boldly asked for goose roasted — is this not the same?"
idiomatic: Liu Yi at Jingkou boldly asked for roast goose — is this not the same?"

literal: You are surely a famed gentleman."
idiomatic: You are surely a famed gentleman."

literal: " Thereafter he always ate with him.
idiomatic: Thereafter they always ate together.

literal: By nature he was square and weighty, loved reading; after wine his pure talk — none who heard but bent the ear.
idiomatic: Square and weighty, he loved books; after wine his pure talk bent every ear.

literal: From Tianbao onward clerical work was prized; those with cultivated bearing were called fallen — Zhan never changed.
idiomatic: From Tianbao clerical work was prized; cultivated bearing was called fallen — Zhan never changed.

literal: He once saw the Selection Office make Liu Di a magistrate and said to them: "A district head should be Zicong's sort — yet you bend a famed man!"
idiomatic: He saw Selection make Liu Di magistrate and said, "A magistrate should be Zicong's sort — yet you bend a famed man!"

literal: " Feng Zicong heard and was greatly angry.
idiomatic: Feng Zicong heard and raged.

literal: When he came to power, Zhan nearly came to ruin.
idiomatic: When Zicong took power Zhan nearly perished.

literal: He had a collection in twenty juan.
idiomatic: He had a collection in twenty juan.

literal: Lin's younger brother Zhongwen had literature.
idiomatic: Lin's brother Zhongwen had letters.

literal: In the Taihe era he was an aide to the Chancellor.
idiomatic: In Taihe he was Chancellor's aide.

literal: At the defeat at Shaye, Zhongwen gripped a horse's tail to cross the river — in the waves now submerged, now surfaced.
idiomatic: At Shaye's defeat Zhongwen gripped a horse's tail to cross — now under the wave, now above.

literal: Shenwu saw from afar and said: "Aide Cui."
idiomatic: Shenwu saw afar and said, "Aide Cui."

literal: " He hastily sent a boat to fetch him.
idiomatic: He sent a boat at once.

literal: When he arrived he said: "You for lord and kin did not spare ten thousand deaths — you may be called the house's filial son and the state's loyal minister."
idiomatic: Arrived, he said, "For lord and kin you did not spare ten thousand deaths — filial son of the house, loyal minister of the state."

literal: Later Wenxiang wished to send him to Qingzhou; hearing he drank much, he stopped.
idiomatic: Later Wenxiang wished to send him to Qing — hearing he drank much, he stopped.

literal: At the start of Tianbao, Lin was Attendant and Zhongwen Silver-Glory Grand Master for Splendid Happiness — the same day they received appointment; clouds showed two phoenixes flying linked.
idiomatic: At Tianbao's start Lin was Attendant and Zhongwen Silver-Glory Grand Master — same day appointed; clouds showed two linked phoenixes.

literal: He was once summoned by edict with overnight wine not yet cleared.
idiomatic: Once summoned by edict with overnight wine uncleared.

literal: Wenxuan was angry and was about to punish him.
idiomatic: Wenxuan raged and was about to punish him.

literal: He was tested with a ten-rhyme poem on viewing the archery contest — brush in hand, it was finished at once — and he was forgiven.
idiomatic: He was tested with ten rhymes on the archery contest — brush in hand, done at once — and forgiven.

literal: He was made Regular Attendant and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: He was made Regular Attendant and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Yan was Groom of the Heir Apparent and Secretariat Officer.
idiomatic: Son Yan was Groom of the Heir Apparent and Secretariat Officer.

literal: Yan's younger brother Biao.
idiomatic: Yan's brother was Biao.

literal: Biao, styled Qishu.
idiomatic: Biao, styled Qishu.

literal: In youth with Lu Sidao of Fanyang and Xin Deyuan of Longxi he shared purpose and friendship.
idiomatic: In youth with Lu Sidao of Fanyang and Xin Deyuan of Longxi he was sworn friend.

literal: He always made reading his task, trusting talent and standing, and wrote large on his door: "Whoever has not read five thousand juan may not enter this room." On first recommendation as cultivated talent he was Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: He made reading his task, trusted talent and rank, and wrote large on his door, "Who has not read five thousand juan may not enter." First recommended as cultivated talent he was Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

literal: He was promoted Attending Censor.
idiomatic: He rose to Attending Censor.

literal: With Xiong Ansheng, Ma Jingde, and others he debated the Five Rites and also revised statutes.
idiomatic: With Xiong Ansheng and Ma Jingde he debated the Five Rites and revised statutes.

literal: Soon he was also Regular Attendant and envoy to Chen.
idiomatic: Soon also Regular Attendant and envoy to Chen.

literal: On return he waited for edicts at the Forest of Literature.
idiomatic: On return he waited for edicts at the Forest of Literature.

literal: He successively was Secretariat Officer.
idiomatic: He was in turn Secretariat Officer.

literal: With Li Ruo of Dunqiu he was alike praised; men of the time said: "In the capital, blazing bright — Cui Biao and Li Ruo."
idiomatic: With Li Ruo of Dunqiu he was alike praised; the age said, "In the capital blazing bright — Cui Biao and Li Ruo."

literal: " Ruo often told his sons: "Lu Sidao and Cui Biao are cliffs far and sheer — they are whom I honor; take them as masters."
idiomatic: Ruo told his sons, "Lu Sidao and Cui Biao are sheer cliffs — honor them; be their pupils."

literal: " Sidao and Biao once bantered after wine; Biao said: "Yan is distant and unheard-of."
idiomatic: Sidao and Biao bantered after wine; Biao said, "Yan is distant and unheard."

literal: " Sidao mocked Biao: "High ancestors' offices were thin."
idiomatic: Sidao mocked Biao, "High ancestors' offices were thin."

literal: When Qi fell he returned home.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he went home.

literal: He served the commandery as Merit Officer and was made Chief Clerk.
idiomatic: He served the commandery as Merit Officer and Chief Clerk.

literal: In the fourth year of Sui Kaihuang he was summoned as Gentleman of the Secretariat and concurrently Palace Secretariat Drafter.
idiomatic: In Sui Kaihuang's fourth year he was summoned Gentleman of the Secretariat and Palace Drafter.

literal: Later he was also Direct Attendant and Regular Attendant and went on embassy to Chen.
idiomatic: Later also Direct Attendant and Regular Attendant on embassy to Chen.

literal: On return he was made Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: On return he was Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
